verdict.rationale: Turso documents creating databases through the CLI (`turso db create`), the Platform API (create, token-scope and tear down per-agent databases), and an official MCP server that lets an agent manage databases and run SQL without copying tokens. Queries can also run through the CLI shell. Retrieving the connection string programmatically is never shown, and applying a schema is only implied by generic SQL execution, so end-to-end coverage is not complete. missing for 10: documented programmatic retrieval of the database URL/connection string, explicit schema-apply/migration workflow via API/CLI/MCP, hands-on corroboration of an agent completing the full flow, published OpenAPI spec (probe 404).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can provision a database end to end — create it, fetch the connection string, apply schema, and run queries — through the API, CLI, or MCP without touching the dashboard

citations.quote: Each entity gets its own isolated SQLite database that you create, token-scope, and tear down via the API.
Connect any MCP-capable AI agent and it can manage your Turso Cloud account — organizations, databases, groups — and run SQL, on your behalf.
Programmatically manage databases, groups, organizations, and tokens with the Turso Platform API.
